name: Steve Ballmer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: Steve Ballmer is the high-energy former CEO of Microsoft, who led the company from 2000 to 2014.
He joined Microsoft in 1980 as employee No. 30 after dropping out of Stanford's MBA program. He first met Microsoft cofounder Bill Gates when the two were undergrads at Harvard.
Ballmer oversaw Microsoft after the first dot-com crash and through efforts to catch up to Google in search capabilities and Apple in mobile phones.
In 2014, the year he retired from Microsoft, he bought the NBA's Los Angeles Clippers for $2 billion; Forbes now values the team at $7.5 billion. He spent another $2 billion building a stadium.
Ballmer, who owned 4% of Microsoft stock when he retired, has held onto most of his stock and has said he's the company's largest individual shareholder.
He has ramped up his philanthropy since 2014; to date the Ballmers have given away more than $6.5 billion.
forbes_facts: Ballmer created a website called USAFacts.org for people to look up and understand where the government is spending money.

name: Dan Friedkin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Dan Friedkin owns Gulf States Toyota, which sold $14.5 billion worth of Toyotas in 2025.
The company, based in Houston, has exclusive rights to distribute Toyota vehicles in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Oklahoma.
His father Thomas, who died in 2017, started the business in 1969.
Through The Friedkin Group, he also owns luxury hospitality management firm Auberge Resorts, which has properties in Aspen and Cabo San Lucas.

NEON, his film studio, won four Academy Awards for "Parasite" in 2020, produced Martin Scorsese's 2023 drama "Flowers Of The Killer Moon" and won five Oscars in 2025 for "Anora." In 2026, the studio's "Sentimental Value" won an Oscar for best international feature.
In 2024, The Friedkin Group acquired fellow billionaire Farhad Moshiri's majority stake in Everton Football Club, the English soccer team.
forbes_facts: His Friedkin Conservation Trust is working to preserve more than 6 million acres in Tanzania.
Friedkin owns one of the largest collections of vintage military war planes in the country.

name: Wang Weixiu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Weixiu's fortune derives from his stake in Zhongji Innolight, a supplier of optical communication modules and devices.
Zhongji Innolight was founded in 1987 and formerly known as Shandong Zhongji Electrical Equipment.
He stepped down as its chairman in 2023.
His son Wang Xiaodong serves as the company's director and executive vice president.

name: Fredrik Lundberg
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Fredrik Lundberg is CEO and chairman of L.E. Lundbergforetagen AB, founded by his father Lars in 1944 as a construction outfit.
Fredrik took over management of the firm in 1981.
Today it's a diversified holding company with investments in property management and other businesses.
Daughters Louise and Katarina, also billionaires, both sit on the board and each own a 15% stake in the group.
Through his holdings, Lundberg has a strong say in a dozen of Sweden's largest firms, including construction company Skanska, pulp and paper companies Holmen, as well as truck-maker Volvo.
forbes_facts: Lundberg moved his family to Switzerland in 1985 to avoid punitive taxes but later returned to Sweden.
Lundberg was once a junior curling world champion.

name: Palmer Luckey
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Wikidata (2015); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Palmer Luckey founded virtual reality company Oculus VR in 2012 and sold it to Facebook in 2014 for $2 billion in cash and stock.
He built the company's first offering, the Oculus Rift virtual reality headset, when he was 16 years old. He left Facebook in 2016.
In 2017, he founded defense startup Anduril, which private investors valued at $30.5 billion in its latest funding round in June 2025.
Luckey grew up in Long Beach, California, where he was home-schooled by his mother and spent time working on cars with his father.
After upgrading old video game consoles to make them mobile, he started collecting bulky VR headsets and tinkering with them.

name: Russ Savage
forbes_bio: Russ Savage founded energy drink company Rockstar in 2001.
Savage sold Rockstar to PepsiCo in 2020, in a deal worth more than $4 billion.
Formerly known as Russ Weiner, he changed his name in 2025 to Russ Savage in honor of his father, right-wing talk-radio star Michael Savage.

He got his start in the late 1990s, when he ran for California State Assembly. Though he lost the race, he caught the eye of his father's friend, Skyy Vodka founder Maurice Kanbar, who quickly hired him.
When Kanbar rejected Savage's idea for an energy drink, he quit and launched Rockstar using a $50,000 mortgage on his Sausalito, Calif. condo.
forbes_facts: Savage started a yard service company in his Northern California neighborhood at age 8 and worked the drive-thru at Wendy's at 15.
Savage once owned a 161-foot yacht named 'Rockstar' that was damaged by a Miami drawbridge.
When the first Rockstar cans hit stores and bars, Savage drove around San Francisco in an old limo painted with the Rockstar logo to promote it.

name: Li Hua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2009-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2020)
forbes_bio: Li Hua, who also goes by Leaf, is the chairman and CEO of Futu Holdings, an online financial services business in China.
The company's investment apps include Futubull for users in China and Moomoo for overseas traders.
Futubull can't sign up new users in mainland China since 2022, when authorities scrutinized its service amid worries of capital outflow and data security.
The company has been expanding internationally in markets including Malaysia, Singapore and the U.S.
Li founded Futu in 2007, after a seven-year stint at Chinese internet giant Tencent, where he held senior management positions.

name: Miguel Fluxa Rossello
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Fluxa Rossello is the executive chairman of Grupo Iberostar, one of Europe's largest hotel companies.
In 2017 Iberostar generated more than $2.9 billion in revenues; it has hotels in 30 countries and 27,100 employees.
The roots of the Iberostar Group date to the 19th century when the Fluxa family started a footwear business in Majorca, Spain.
In 1986 Miguel joined the family company, which was still small, and founded the first Iberostar hotels in Majorca and the Canary Islands.
In 2006 he sold the group's tour operator and travel agency divisions to the Carlyle Group for $950 million.
forbes_facts: His grandfather, Antonio Fluxa, set up the family's footwear business in 1877 and within a decade, it had 11 workshops and five leather factories.
